static_findings.snippet: - Use consolidated metadata to reduce latency: `zarr.consolidate_metadata(store)`
- Speeds up `tree()` operations and group traversal
- **Balance**: Larger chunks = fewer metadata operations; smaller chunks = better parallel access

content.value_statement: Large scientific arrays are hard to store, chunk, and move across local and cloud systems. This skill guides Zarr Python setup, chunking, compression, storage backends, and integrations with NumPy, Dask, and Xarray.
actual_capabilities: Create and open Zarr arrays and groups with chunked storage.
Choose chunk sizes and shapes for common access patterns.
Configure compression codecs such as Blosc, Zstandard, Gzip, and BytesCodec.
Use local, memory, ZIP, S3, and Google Cloud Storage backends.
Integrate Zarr data with NumPy, Dask, and Xarray workflows.
Troubleshoot performance, memory use, cloud latency, and concurrent writes.
limitations: Does not execute, benchmark, or validate code examples automatically.
Cloud examples require valid credentials and optional storage packages.
Does not replace official Zarr API documentation for every version detail.
Users must adapt paths, chunk sizes, and credentials to their own environment.

use_cases.title: Design a scientific data store
use_cases.description: Plan chunking, compression, and hierarchy for large climate, imaging, or simulation arrays.

use_cases.title: Move arrays to cloud storage
use_cases.description: Map Zarr stores to S3 or Google Cloud Storage with metadata settings for faster reads.

use_cases.title: Optimize analysis workflows
use_cases.description: Combine Zarr with Dask or Xarray for lazy loading, parallel computation, and labeled datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Create my first Zarr array
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a local array store.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a local Zarr array for a two-dimensional float dataset. Explain chunk size, dtype, and read/write mode choices.

prompt_templates.title: Choose chunking and compression
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my array shape, dtype, and access pattern. Recommend chunk shape, chunk size, compression codec, and tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a cloud storage workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Zarr workflow for S3 or Google Cloud Storage. Include store setup, metadata consolidation, sharding, and latency considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a slow Zarr pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze why my Zarr workload is slow or memory heavy. Consider chunk alignment, compression, consolidated metadata, and Dask scheduling.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to store a 10,000 by 10,000 float array locally.
output: Recommends a Zarr array with explicit shape, dtype, and square chunks.
Explains why chunk size should balance memory use and read patterns.
Notes when compression helps and when it may slow interactive reads.

output_examples.input: A user wants to read climate data from object storage with Xarray.
output: Suggests a cloud-backed Zarr store with consolidated metadata.
Explains lazy loading through Xarray and Dask.
Highlights credential, chunk size, and object request considerations.

output_examples.input: A user reports high memory use during Zarr processing.
output: Identifies full-array reads and oversized chunks as likely causes.
Recommends chunk-wise processing or Dask-backed computation.
Warns that shards and chunks must fit within available memory.

best_practices: Choose chunks from real read and write patterns, not only total array size.
Use consolidated metadata for large hierarchical stores, especially on cloud storage.
Document compression, sharding, and storage backend choices with each dataset.
anti_patterns: Do not load an entire large array into memory when chunk-wise reads are enough.
Do not use very small chunks for cloud workloads without sharding or metadata planning.
Do not assume concurrent writes are safe without synchronizers or non-overlapping chunks.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design and troubleshoot Zarr Python arrays, groups, compression, storage backends, and analysis integrations.

faq.question: Does it support cloud storage?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers S3 and Google Cloud Storage patterns through s3fs and gcsfs examples.

faq.question: Can it help choose chunk sizes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains chunk size and shape tradeoffs based on memory, access pattern, and storage backend.

faq.question: Does it run benchmarks?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example workflows, but users must benchmark in their own environment.

faq.question: Which Python tools does it mention?
faq.answer: It covers NumPy, Dask, Xarray, s3fs, gcsfs, h5py, and Zarr storage classes.

faq.question: Is it only for scientists?
faq.answer: No. It is useful for any team storing large multidimensional arrays or chunked analytical datasets.
